subject.title: [Feature]: models.providers.*.enabled flag to disable providers without removing config

question: Should OpenClaw add a public `models.providers.<id>.enabled?: boolean` contract, and what should happen when the disabled provider is the selected primary?
rationale: Source inspection proves the gap, but the requested fix adds public config surface and changes provider-routing/fallback semantics that require maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve shared provider eligibility
options.body: Add the config field and one shared eligibility helper across schema, planning, fallback, catalogs, status/probe output, docs, and tests, including disabled-primary semantics.

options.title: Reject provider-level disable
options.body: Keep the current model where operators remove provider blocks or adjust model/fallback config, avoiding another public config knob.

options.title: Defer to provider lifecycle design
options.body: Hold this until provider enable/disable, plugin setup, auth/status, and model picker lifecycle behavior are designed together.

recommendation.title: Approve shared provider eligibility
recommendation.body: Add the config field and one shared eligibility helper across schema, planning, fallback, catalogs, status/probe output, docs, and tests, including disabled-primary semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across the central model/provider config, fallback, catalog, and status paths that would own the shared contract.
